reason: The cited evidence shows that rapid synthesis can produce homogeneous HEA nanoparticles (E2) and that such nanoparticles can be thermally stable (E3), but none of the passages provide data on how mixing versus segregation affects cohesive energy, premelting onset, or melting temperature. The key mechanistic premises linking mixing to melting behavior are therefore unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: Uniform atomic mixing in HEA nanoparticles enhances inter-element bonding and cohesive energy
Local elemental segregation creates weakly bound surface regions that promote premelting
Higher cohesive energy from mixing delays surface premelting and raises melting temperature
Nanoparticle size below ~10 nm ensures surface energy effects dominate melting behavior
Rapid synthesis methods (e.g., fast moving bed pyrolysis) can produce homogeneously mixed HEA nanoparticles
